en: The Sūtra on King Vaiśravaṇa Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master for the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fǎtián, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa...
Together with a retinue of hundreds of thousands of countless yakṣas,
they came to the Buddha’s dwelling during the first watch of the night,
emitting a great radiance that illuminated the entire precinct of the Jeta Grove.
Prostrating with his five limbs to the ground, he paid homage at the feet of the World-Honored One.
Standing to one side, he joined his palms toward the Buddha and praised him in verse:
"I take refuge in the Great Fearless One, The Perfectly Awakened, the Honored One among bipeds."
With their divine eyes, the devas behold me;
I have seen the Buddhas of the past, present, and future, The Lords of Compassion throughout the three times, Each and every One-Who-Knows-All-Things.
To them, I now pay homage with my life surrendered.
At that time, after the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa had spoken these verses,
he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
there are śrāvakas— bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās."
Whether walking, sitting, or lying down in the wilderness, in forests, or at the foot of trees,
I am this yakṣa, a non-human being.
There are those who have faith in the Buddha’s words, and there are those who have but little faith.
Furthermore, there are countless malevolent yakṣas who do not believe in the Buddha’s words;
they harass and disturb sentient beings, causing them to dwell in insecurity.
Excellent, World-Honored One! May all the Aṭānāṭīya Sūtras serve as a clear protection.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, as well as devas and humans,
who receive, uphold, read, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain it to others;
They are all able to provide protection and bring about auspiciousness.
At that time, there was a multitude of yakṣas of right faith within the assembly who,
with palms joined, addressed [the Buddha], saying:
"We only pray that the Heavenly King will preach this sutra; we long to hear it.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa silently accepted the request and immediately went before the Buddha, prostrating himself with his head at the Buddha's feet.
Relying on the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, he addressed the yakṣas, saying:
"If this sutra is obtained and proclaimed for circulation,
it will be able to eliminate all the afflictions of sentient beings."
Therefore, I now take refuge in and pay homage to him.
In the eastern world, there is a Gandharva lord named Dhṛtarāṣṭra,
who possesses great majesty and virtue, and whose body radiates light.
It is like the rising sun that universally illuminates the world;
presiding over his retinue, surrounded by a respectful assembly of gandharvas,
he experiences joy through song, dance, and music.
He had ninety-one sons, all named Śakra,
who possessed great power and were fierce and violent;
yet, upon seeing the Buddha, the World-Honored One, they took refuge in him, prostrated themselves, and revered and honored him with deep respect.
Observe that even though he is not a human, he is able to pay homage and respect.
That Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra protects the eastern direction;
he guards the world just as the Buddha practices his conduct.
Therefore, I now prostrate and take refuge in the Perfectly Enlightened One, the One Endowed with Knowledge and Conduct, the Unsurpassed Peace.
In the southern world, there is a lord of kumbhāṇḍas named Vīrudhaka.
Possessing great majestic power, his body radiates light;
like the sun illuminating the world, he is as deep, vast, and boundless as the great ocean,
such that all ordinary beings cannot fathom him.
Surrounded by his retinue and a host of kumbhāṇḍas who pay him respectful homage,
he enjoys happiness through singing, dancing, and chanting.
He has ninety-one sons, all of whom share the same name, Śakra.
Possessing great power and being fierce and violent,
upon seeing the Buddha, the World-Honored One, he took refuge in him, prostrated, and paid him respect and honor;
observing that this non-human being was able to pay such homage, [he was moved].
That Lord of the Kumbhāṇḍas protects the southern direction;
he guards the world just as the Buddha acts when walking.
Therefore, I now bow my head and take refuge in the One of Right and Universal Knowledge, Perfect in Wisdom and Conduct, the Unsurpassed Peace.
In the western world, there is a great lord of nāgas named Varuṇa.
Possessing great majesty and splendor that shines afar,
he is respectfully surrounded by his retinue and the great hosts of nāgas.
They enjoyed themselves through singing, dancing, and chanting.
They had ninety-one sons, all named Śakra,
who possessed great power and were fierce and violent.
Seeing the Buddha, the World-Honored One, they took refuge in him, prostrated, and paid him respect with deep reverence;
observing that even this non-human being was able to pay such homage,
[they realized] that great Nāga Lord protects the western direction.
Just as the Buddha practices his conduct, so does he protect the world.
Therefore, I now prostrate and take refuge in the Perfectly All-Knowing One, the One Endowed with Knowledge and Conduct, the Unsurpassed Peace.
In the northern world, there is a yakṣa named Kubera.
Possessing great majesty and virtue, his bodily radiance blazed intensely like a great flame.
Surrounded by a retinue of yakṣas whom he commanded with reverence,
he enjoyed happiness through singing, dancing, and music.
He had ninety-one sons, all named Śakra,
who possessed great power and were fierce and violent;
yet, upon seeing the Buddha, the World-Honored One, they took refuge in him, prostrated themselves, and honored him with deep respect.
Observing that even this non-human being is able to pay homage and respect to that Lord of Yakṣas who protects the northern quarter,
and who guards the world just as the Buddha practices his conduct— therefore,
I now bow my head and take refuge in the One Perfectly and Fully Enlightened, Endowed with Knowledge and Conduct, the Unsurpassed Peace.
Furthermore, in the world of the northern direction,
the human lifespan is one thousand years, and no one dies prematurely;
the earth requires no cultivation, and people do not engage in manual labor.
Food and drink appear spontaneously, endowed with perfect color and fragrance;
they nourish the sense faculties, and the body becomes radiant and supple.
Everywhere there are trees bearing flowers and fruit, as well as flowing springs and ponds.
They sport at will as if experiencing celestial bliss.
Thus it is with Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the east, Virūḍhaka in the south,
Virūpākṣa in the west, and Kubera in the north.
Each protects the four great continents by means of their own majestic power.
Furthermore, among the lords of the gandharvas,
there is a host of yakṣiṇīs who ride upon elephants.
Some rode horses, some rode camels;
some rode water buffaloes, some rode sheep;
some rode snakes, and some rode birds.
Some were mounted on young boys, and some were mounted on young girls;
led by elephants in front,
they traveled secretly through various directions across the void.
They manifest various transformations with sovereign ease according to their will,
and they are also able to protect others while remaining invisible.
Furthermore, the yakṣas may have various forms that are hideous and diverse.
They are also like birds that travel through the void,
roaming with sovereign ease and providing secret protection for people.
Their names are Aṭaṇāṭa, Kuṇāṭa, Parikuśanāṭa, Nāṇa, Nāṇa, and Pṛika, among others.
Together with the hosts of yakṣiṇīs,
they all reside in the great city of Aṭakāvatī in the north.
Furthermore, within this great city, there is a palace.
On its four sides there are ninety-nine ponds;
their waters are exceedingly deep and vast, and they are called Earth Ponds (*bhūmi-kuṇḍa*).
Their springs flow through channels and are also capable of raining down water.
Furthermore, there are many kinds of flowering and fruit-bearing trees,
namely the *kovidāra*, *kuraṇṭaka*, *campaka*, and other such flowers;
their fruits are sweet in taste and are cherished by all.
Various birds, such as kalaviṅkas and peacocks, constantly utter exquisite sounds.
There is a son of heaven named Vīra who,
together with his retinue, also dwells in this palace to protect the realm.
Then, King Vaiśravaṇa, empowered by the compassionate strength of the Buddha, proclaimed the mantra in succession, saying:
*Tadyathā | i-li mi-li i-le kintamaule hi-le kintimau-le hana-mi hu-nu-ri nu-mi kau-ri ghan-da-ri gu-nu-hi-ni u-khi hu-khi svāhā*. At that time, King Vaiśravaṇa had finished reciting the mantra.
He addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One, there are also many great gandharvas who are my brothers."

Their names were: Kāmadarśa, Rati-darśa, Gītamada, Māramada, Madhumada, Puṣpamada, Nityamada, Śrī-mada, Dhana-mada, Dhanika, Utpala, Padma, Candrārddha, Nīlakuñjara, Siddhamūla, Pañca-śikha, Varṇa-varṇa, Kanakamaṇi, Viśvakuṭṭima-hāsa, Bhūpati, Jayagata, and Indragati.
Such gandharva hosts as these delude and afflict all sentient beings;
if there are those who afflict sentient beings and do not abandon such conduct, [they shall be restrained].
Upon hearing this mantra, one’s head shall split into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree. The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā | gautali gautarale hīṣaṇe maṇḍike saṇapāṇike tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha mānuṣye svāhā*. Blessed One, if there be any śrāvakas—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—[who encounter this, they shall be protected].
If one upholds, recites, honors, makes offerings to, and extensively explains this sutra for others,
then those gandharvas, along with their parents, brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and retinues [will be protected].
None of them will be able to cause harm;
they shall constantly come to attend upon, serve, and protect [the practitioner].
Should anyone attempt to afflict or harm them, they will immediately lose their majestic power.
He shall not attain the Gandharva Samādhi;
his head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
Furthermore, he shall not go to dwell in the great city of Aṇāvakāśa.
Blessed One, if there should be any śrāvakas— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās— who receive, uphold, read, recite,
pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain this sūtra for the sake of others.
Neither Piśācas, nor their parents, brothers, sons, daughters, or retinues will be able to cause them harm;
they shall constantly approach, attend upon, and protect them.
Should anyone seek to afflict or harm them, that person’s power and majesty shall immediately vanish.
One must not enter the Samādhi of the Closed House on the Left;
one's head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree, nor shall one go to dwell in the great city of Aṇāvakāśa.
The mantra is:
*tadyathā | hūmi hūmi hūmilavateye svāhā*. Furthermore, O World-Honored One, there is a host of kumbhāṇḍas.

Their names were Nanda and Upananda; Kṛkī, Hakeśu, Mahāpraśu, Mahānala, Naśaha, Sudrūmi, Zarumata, Kṛṣṇaruci, Aparāvarta, Vimardini, Garjara, Jarjarudana, Nanināli, Cūḍanāga, Māgama, Māgeyara, Khañja, Kṛyayu, Pandatraya, Kinnara, Vānari, Sarvarañgacitraku, and so forth.
Such are the hosts of kumbhāṇḍas who delude and afflict all sentient beings;
if any such afflictors hear this mantra, [they shall be subdued].
May their heads split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
The mantra is:
*Tadyathā | siri visiri siri visiri kṛṣṇa tsaga le karani piṅga le svāhā*. World-Honored One, if there be any śrāvakas—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—[who oppose this].
Regarding this sutra, those who receive,
uphold, read, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain it to others—
along with their hosts of kumbhāṇḍas, as well as their parents, brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and retinues— [shall all attain peace].
None of them will be able to cause harm;
they shall constantly come to attend upon, serve, and protect [the practitioner].
Should anyone attempt to afflict or harm them, they will immediately lose their power and majesty.
If one cannot [attain] the Kumbhāṇḍa Samādhi,
one’s head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree,
and one shall not be permitted to go and dwell within the great city of Aṇāvakāśī.
Blessed One, if there should be any śrāvakas— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās— who receive, uphold, read, recite,
pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain this sūtra for others;
Neither that bhūta nor its parents, brothers, sons, daughters,
or retinue will be able to cause harm; rather,
they will constantly come to draw near, attend upon, and make offerings to them.
If there is anyone who causes harm or affliction, they shall immediately lose their majestic power and fail to attain the Bhr̥kuṭī-samādhi;
their head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an Āmalaka tree.
Furthermore, one must not go to dwell within the great city of Aṇāvakāṭī.
The mantra is:
*tadyathā | yume yume liyume lavadeye svāhā*. World-Honored One, I shall now further speak of the various hosts of great nāgas.
Their names were: Nanu, Pananu, Nanīva, Vasuki, Balin, Jāṅguli, Garuḍa, Dīrghakarṇa,
Indravāhu, Śāstika, Aśvakuṇḍita, Śuka, Vipramukta, Jvalanaprabha, Bhṛmida, and Citra.
Tārabiriḥ tvaṃ jītara prahava ji mahāpanisora-jayuti rasu mahā-ṛṣiṇa-bhūrja-gam āryapra-takṣava-ma.
*Kṛṣṇaśāśayamāṭku*, and so forth, up to "those who practice in the world.
In this way, these nāgas and others harass sentient beings.
Upon hearing this mantra, one’s head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
The mantra is as follows:

*tadyathā | jile vijile jile vijile yuri khandali mandini caṇḍāli svāhā*. World-Honored One, if there be any śrāvakas—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—[who encounter this, they shall be protected].
Those among the host of nāgas, as well as their parents,
brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and retinues, who uphold, read, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain this sūtra for others— [they shall all attain liberation].
None of them will be able to cause harm;
they shall constantly come to attend upon, serve, and protect [the practitioner].
Should anyone seek to afflict or harm them, that person will immediately lose their power and majesty.
If you do not attain the *nāga-madhyama-samādhi*,
your head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree;
furthermore, you shall not be permitted to go and dwell in the great city of Aṇāvakāśa.
Blessed One, if there should be any śrāvakas— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās— who receive, uphold, read, recite,
pay homage to, make offerings to, and extensively explain this sūtra for others;
Neither that Kaṭapūtana nor his parents, brothers, sons, daughters,
or retinue will be able to cause him harm;
they will constantly come to attend upon, serve, and make offerings to him.
If there should be anyone who causes harm or affliction,
they shall immediately lose their majestic power and fail to attain the Kakkhaṭatana-samādhi;
their head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an ari tree.
Nor can they go to dwell within the great city of Aṇāvakarṣaṭī.
The mantra is:
*tadyathā āveśaya vaideye svāhā*. O Bhagavān, I shall now describe those yakṣa generals.
Their names were Indrasūmbarudra-prajāpati-bhānava-īśāna-cakranābha.
Kāmaśīlā-kūṇi-jaḍhuḥ.
Nimuṇḍe maṇili maṇili maṇijvālāpradīpane.
Upabhañjaka-satagiri-hima-vadabruna-khane-ira-kuvita-yuparaya-ksa.
Aṭavakunārarājūḍe nīlasapācitrasenāgandhari-vau.
Nirgrantha-śāktī-mātṛ-pañcālaka-jñāna-somanirgrāya-kṣa,
together with all your retinues, Tṛphale!
From Vajrāṅkuśī and the others of the left [retinue],
up to the worldly practitioners, all are members of the retinue.
If they should disturb or harass sentient beings and not desist, [one should act].
Upon hearing this mantra, one’s head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā | hile mile hīmīle kṛte mūle hile kṛte mūle oṃ doṃmi doṃmi udome udomi ukiṃ kiṃ gurnu hiṃ buraṅgali sistaṃtani svāhā.* World-Honored One, if there should be any śrāvakas—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—[who encounter this].
Those yakṣas, along with their parents, brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and retinues,
who uphold, read, recite, pay homage to, make offerings to,
and extensively explain this sūtra for others— [they shall be protected].
None of these can cause harm.
Should anyone disturb or harass [the practitioner], they will immediately lose their majestic power and be unable to attain the yakṣa-samādhi.
Their heads shall be split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree,
and they shall not be able to go to dwell within the great city of Aṇḍhakāvatī.
World-Honored One, if there are any śrāvakas— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās— [who act thus].
Those rākṣasas, along with their parents, brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and retinues, who uphold, read, recite,
pay homage to, make offerings to,
and extensively explain this sūtra for others— [they shall all attain liberation].
None of them can cause harm;
they will constantly come to attend upon, serve, and make offerings to him.
Should anyone attempt to disturb or harass him, that person will immediately lose their majestic power.
If one cannot attain the Rākṣasa-samādhi,
one’s head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an ari tree,
and one shall likewise be unable to go and dwell within the great city of Aṇakāvatī.
The mantra is:
*Tadyathā* | *hile hile* | *hulu hulu* | *yume yume* | *ravaṭe ye* | *svāhā*. After the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa had spoken this Aṭānāṭīya Sūtra, [he sat down].
Having prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, he withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, during the middle of the night, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
Thus, this sutra possesses great power and can serve as a protective illumination.
That King Vaiśravaṇa, together with his retinue of countless hundreds of thousands of yakṣas,
emits a great radiance that illuminates the entire precinct of the Jeta Grove.
He spoke these verses:
"I take refuge in the Great Fearless One, The Perfectly Awakened, the Honored One among bipeds.
With their divine eyes, the devas searched for me but saw nothing."
The Buddhas of the past and future, the Lords of compassion throughout the three times,
each and every one a Samyaksaṃbuddha— to them I now pay homage with this verse.
Having spoken these verses, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
There were certain śrāvaka bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who were walking, sitting,
or lying down in the open wilderness, among the forests, or at the foot of trees;
there were also various yakṣas and non-human beings.
There are those who believe the Buddha’s words, those with little faith,
and those who are extremely wicked and faithless;
they harass and disturb sentient beings, causing them to dwell in insecurity.
I shall expound this sutra for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings.
You bhikṣus, listen closely, listen closely!
This sutra possesses true and great majestic power, capable of providing protection and refuge.
"Furthermore, gods and humans shall always receive secret protection.
You should uphold this and propagate it widely.
Having spoken these words, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa Spoken by the Buddha
